reivew this trail https://entire.io/gh/entireio/cli/trails/1073/feat-self-heal-zombie-sessions-via-detached-sweep-from and this comment specifically Reviewed alongside trail 1061 / PR #2013 (identity-based commit linking). Two things worth knowing before either lands.

**Merge: clean except one docs hunk.** I test-merged the two branches — every Go file auto-merges (including `strategy/manual_commit_session.go`, which both touch: 1061 edits `exactWorktreeMatches`/`findSessionsForWorktree` at 171-290, this branch renames `isWarnableStaleEndedSession` → `IsCondensableEndedSession` at 128-160, adjacent but non-overlapping). The only conflict is `docs/architecture/sessions-and-checkpoints.md`, where both insert a paragraph at the same anchor after the session-adopt section. Whoever lands second just rebases that hunk.

**`SessionState.Owner` is becoming a single point of failure for three behaviours.** It already carries liveness; 1061 makes it carry commit attribution, and this branch makes it decide whether background repair work gets spawned at all. It is nil on Windows, and nil whenever `proclive.ResolveOwner` walks only transient ancestors (manual_commit_hooks.go:2478-2481 clears it and degrades silently by design).

Both branches degrade correctly when it is nil — 1061 falls back to worktree matching, this one just does not spawn. But the *value* of both features is directly proportional to a resolve rate nobody has measured. Do we have any signal on how often `ResolveOwner` succeeds across the supported agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot CLI, Gemini, OpenCode, Pi, Factory Droid)? The transient list (proclive.go:88-100) is tuned for `entire`/shells/`go`, and the comment there notes interpreter runtimes were deliberately left off because "for several agents the runtime IS the long-lived agent" — which is a judgement call per agent, currently unverified per agent. A one-off count of non-nil `Owner` across real session states would tell us whether these features are load-bearing or decorative on the agents we actually ship for.

- The useful review question is therefore twofold: whether `Owner` is semantically trustworthy, and whether its resolution rate is observable across real agent process trees.

- I’m now checking capture behavior and per-agent launch trees so the response is precise rather than merely agreeing with the concern.

Entire Review:

Reviewing [trail 1073](https://entire.io/gh/entireio/cli/trails/1073) / [PR #2029](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2029): 11 commits, 15 files changed. Intent context was available from the trail checkpoint.

No blocking implementation defect found. The targeted sweep/finalization tests pass. Entire’s Findings gate also passes; the gate is red only because no reviewer has approved it. GitHub currently marks the PR conflicted.

Medium: `SessionState.Owner` lacks supported-agent validation.

- The comment’s central concern is valid: no telemetry or test matrix currently measures `ResolveOwner` across all supported agent process trees.
- Local state provides encouraging but incomplete evidence: excluding legacy fixtures, owner capture succeeded for 10/10 Claude Code and 7/7 Codex turn-bearing sessions on macOS.
- The single Cursor state had no owner, but it also never reached TurnStart, so it did not exercise `ResolveOwner`.
- There is no evidence here for Copilot CLI, Gemini, OpenCode, Pi, or Factory Droid. Windows is unsupported by design.

One important qualification: `Owner` is not a complete single point of failure for PR #2029. The ENDED-session repair path—the motivating zombie case—does not use it. A missing owner disables automatic repair of non-ended sessions whose process vanished; `status` and `doctor` retain the one-hour stale fallback, but the detached SessionStart sweep does not. PR #2013 similarly falls back to worktree matching.

The merge claim is correct: merging PR #2013 and #2029 produces actual conflict markers only in `docs/architecture/sessions-and-checkpoints.md`; their overlapping Go files merge automatically.

Comment I would post:

> Good call. We don’t currently have a cross-agent success-rate signal for `ResolveOwner`, so there isn’t a representative number to point to yet.
>
> I did the one-off state count suggested here. Excluding legacy fixture states, this macOS repo has `Owner` on 10/10 Claude Code and 7/7 Codex turn-bearing sessions. The one Cursor state has no owner, but it never recorded a TurnStart, so it doesn’t tell us whether `ResolveOwner` would have succeeded. We have no sample here for Copilot CLI, Gemini, OpenCode, Pi, or Factory Droid, and Windows is unsupported by design.
>
> One nuance: `Owner` is a shared optimization hinge rather than a correctness single point of failure. In #2029, the ENDED-and-uncondensed repair path is independent of `Owner`; nil only disables immediate repair of non-ended sessions whose agent process vanished. `status`/`doctor` still use the inactivity fallback, although the detached SessionStart sweep does not. #2013 likewise falls back to worktree matching.
>
> So the concern is valid, especially for the ACTIVE-zombie half of #2029 and the incremental value of #2013. I don’t think it blocks #2029’s motivating ENDED-zombie fix, but we should run a macOS/Linux acceptance matrix across the supported agents before treating owner-based behavior as a reliable cross-agent guarantee. A diagnostic should record only agent type, platform, and resolve success—not PID or process details.
